The elevator list calls this the SUMMIT, subway and Grand Central Terminal level. Its depth is this app's usual one storey below the street: assumed. Opening and landing construction is illustrative: 0.65 m end plates, 2.5 m opening headroom, guard profiles and door thresholds are not surveyed dimensions. Existing source tiers and equipment endpoints are retained. The outline is the MTA's, with a margin: it is not the walls.

18 ft (official escalator rise) below the street at Park and Lexington, plus 3.4 m for the fall of 42nd St between there and Vanderbilt Ave. Wikipedia gives the Shuttle as about 20 ft (6.1 m) deep; it is drawn on this level because the passage joins them without a machine. Opening and landing construction is illustrative: 0.65 m end plates, 2.5 m opening headroom, guard profiles and door thresholds are not surveyed dimensions. Existing source tiers and equipment endpoints are retained. The outline is the MTA's, with a margin: it is not the walls.

Depth assumed, the deepest that clears the western mezzanine for the 7 below it, whose depth is official: tracks 1.2 m below the platform and 2.3 m of headroom under them. Opening and landing construction is illustrative: 0.65 m end plates, 2.5 m opening headroom, guard profiles and door thresholds are not surveyed dimensions.
